requirement: Each evidence detail page MUST display its state as a Shields.io static badge image with meaningful alt text and the current requirement or example body as a Markdown block quote labeled by kind. It MUST render the recorded rationale as Markdown in a Rationale section and display the recorded FIXME strings when the determination is FIXME. Inputs MUST be grouped under headings in this order, each input appearing once, in the first group that applies to it: Implementation, for sources reached by an `{impl}` edge from the definition, including anchored files; Tests, for sources reached by a `{test}` edge, including tests, examples, and anchored files; Referenced definitions, for declarations the definition cites and their terminology; and Other sources, for the remaining inputs the assessment consulted. Edges MUST be determined from the current references under {cite}`requirements.references.roles` and {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`. Each group and each input MUST be a collapsible disclosure element, with groups expanded and inputs collapsed by default, so readers can move between groups and open individual sources. Each input MUST have its own subsection identifying its selector. An outline input MUST show its file, selector, kind, and current inclusive line range. A requirements input MUST show its selection and each matched definition's full name, file, and inclusive line range. Each outline input subsection MUST show the node's current source text in a fenced code block and say when its hash no longer matches; a requirements or definition input subsection MUST show its recorded text. Code fences MUST request Rust highlighting for `.rs` files and language-aware highlighting for Markdown, JSON, TOML, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python files; TOML MAY use INI highlighting when native TOML highlighting is unavailable.

text: :::{req} detail_format

Each evidence detail page MUST display its state as a Shields.io static badge image with meaningful alt text and the current requirement or example body as a Markdown block quote labeled by kind. It MUST render the recorded rationale as Markdown in a Rationale section and display the recorded FIXME strings when the determination is FIXME. Inputs MUST be grouped under headings in this order, each input appearing once, in the first group that applies to it: Implementation, for sources reached by an `{impl}` edge from the definition, including anchored files; Tests, for sources reached by a `{test}` edge, including tests, examples, and anchored files; Referenced definitions, for declarations the definition cites and their terminology; and Other sources, for the remaining inputs the assessment consulted. Edges MUST be determined from the current references under {cite}`requirements.references.roles` and {cite}`requirements.references.anchors`. Each group and each input MUST be a collapsible disclosure element, with groups expanded and inputs collapsed by default, so readers can move between groups and open individual sources. Each input MUST have its own subsection identifying its selector. An outline input MUST show its file, selector, kind, and current inclusive line range. A requirements input MUST show its selection and each matched definition's full name, file, and inclusive line range. Each outline input subsection MUST show the node's current source text in a fenced code block and say when its hash no longer matches; a requirements or definition input subsection MUST show its recorded text. Code fences MUST request Rust highlighting for `.rs` files and language-aware highlighting for Markdown, JSON, TOML, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python files; TOML MAY use INI highlighting when native TOML highlighting is unavailable.
:::{req} roles

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name, or with a built-in name under {cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, and MAY use the `{fixme}` role in fenced form. A reference MAY instead be written in fenced form, `:::{role} name` on one line, a body, and a closing fence, following the fence rules of {cite}`requirements.ci.span` and {cite}`requirements.ci.fence_lengths`; the fenced form is the same edge with attached commentary, and the inline form carries none. In a source comment, fence lines MUST be recognized after removing each line's comment delimiters within one comment run under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, and a fence that does not close within its comment run MUST be a validation error. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a project source item or a requirement or example declaration. The roles MUST mean:
- `{cite}`: the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition. It is an
edge from the source to the definition.
- `{impl}`: the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision,
performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition
specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining
one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or
producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as
implementing it. A check MUST count only if the definition states it, or the
source could not meet one of the definition's obligations without it; source
that checks it is consistent with a definition, such as recognizing a form the
definition specifies in order to decide whether to run other behavior, relies
on that definition and calls for `{cite}`. A requirement stating a convention
for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by
the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that
collects and reports those outputs.
- `{test}`: the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies:
a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome,
or a named example through the concrete case it describes.
- `{fixme}`: the source acknowledges a known gap in fulfilling the definition. It
MUST use the fenced form, and its body MUST describe the gap. The body MAY
begin with option lines naming issues that track the gap, one per line, in the
form `:github: <owner>/<repo>#<number>`, such as
`:github: rust-lang/rust#123`. `github` MUST be the only recognized option.
A named `{fixme}` MAY appear only in sources outside the book. Validation MUST report
any other option line, a `:github:` value not in that form, an inline
`{fixme}`, a `{fixme}` in a requirement or example declaration, and a
`{fixme}` whose body, without option lines and comment delimiters, is empty.
An unnamed `{fixme}`, a fence of `:::{fixme}` with no name, MAY appear in any
project text, including a requirement or example body, to tie that place to
the issues it names. It MUST have at least one `:github:` option line and MAY
have a description; it is not a reference edge, acknowledges no gap, needs no
coverage, and does not count as a reference for Rust item coverage. Its
issues are checked under {cite}`requirements.cli.fixme_issues`.
`{impl}`, `{test}`, and `{fixme}` are edges from the definition to the source.
Only requirements and examples are assessed; code is reviewed as part of the
definitions it implements or tests.
```text
{impl}`requirements.references.roles`
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`
{test}`requirements.references.roles`
:::{req} anchors
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.
An anchored file or node MUST be covered by the definition's evidence under
{cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`, by an input selecting it, so changing the file makes that evidence stale. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference, because the
definition cannot be assessed without it. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.
